beats.say: One agent with fifty tools and a giant prompt gets confused. Splitting the work across specialized agents often works better.
In the orchestrator-worker pattern, a planner agent splits the task, sends subtasks to workers, and combines their results.
Workers run in parallel, which saves time. The planner waits for all of them, or takes the first good answer.
But workers fail and time out. So the planner needs timeouts, retries, and a fallback, so one stuck worker doesn't block everything.

beats.text: Small, explicit hand-offs. Log every message.
beats.say: Agents share state through messages or a shared store. Keep hand-offs small and explicit, and log every message.

beats.text: More agents = more tokens, latency, failures.
beats.say: The cost: more agents means more tokens, more latency, and more ways to fail. Start with one agent, and split only when you must.
